terra.problem: “Frog for frog” suggests the magicians produced the same number of frogs as Aaron. The text does not give their numbers.
The text does not say Pharaoh could have had the frogs gone that day or establish that they remained for one more night.
“Frogs until then” adds a timing detail the text does not give. Pharaoh chooses when Moses will pray.
“They didn't go anywhere” conflicts with the next verse, which says the dead frogs were piled into heaps.
“Pharaoh heard them out” conflicts with the text's statement that he would not listen to Moses and Aaron.
“The offer is forgotten” claims to know Pharaoh's thoughts. The text says he would not listen, not that he forgot his offer.
The dust asking for a job is an unrelated joke that does not pass the joke logic test.
“That's all the text gives” overlooks what the passage says about the dust turning into gnats.
The text does not say the dust is still turning into gnats while the magicians try. It says the gnats remained on man and beast.
“There's no half-credit in this one” jokes about the question itself.
“They said so” suggests the magicians told Pharaoh they could not copy the gnats. The text says they called it the finger of God.
The magicians did not tell Pharaoh the same thing as Moses and Aaron. They said it was the finger of God.
